CLAIMS.CLAIM_TEXT: Answers LAB-Q-0016 ('what structural biases would a future Job Posting Observatory carry?') as a design-stage pre-mortem, using exclusively this phase's own Observatory design (reports/lab_c0/LAB-C0-observatory-design.json); no platform was selected, no data was captured. Finding: yes, substantial and structurally unavoidable biases across eight dimensions. Platform selection: over-represents the eventually-chosen platform's own user base, under-represents employers using other channels (direct career pages, referrals, niche boards, or no formal posting at all). Sector coverage: over-represents white-collar/digital-native roles relative to informal, manual, rural, or micro-enterprise hiring. Geography: skews toward high-connectivity urban areas. Seniority: a near-certain skew whose direction is not determinable without data. Duplicates: the same vacancy can be counted more than once absent a platform-issued stable identifier -- disclosed and flagged by the design's own dedup taxonomy, not resolved by it. Posting persistence: long-lived postings are structurally over-represented by snapshot-design construction alone, independent of their true relative frequency. Employer self-selection: only employers who post formally, on a captured platform, are observed at all. Posting-vs-real-hiring divergence: structurally unresolvable by this design, since it never observes VACANCY or HIRE -- this is LAB-Q-0018's own separate, unresolved question. None of these biases block LAB-Q-0014 itself, which asks only what posting text alone can reveal; they must, however, be disclosed in full alongside any future LAB-Q-0014 finding.
LIMITATIONS: Qualitative, design-stage reasoning only; no corpus exists, so no actual bias magnitude is measured or claimed

CLAIMS.CLAIM_TEXT: LAB-Q-0018 ('when both are observable, how do descriptions based on published job postings diverge from descriptions based on real hiring outcomes?') is closed INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE on source-availability grounds, without any new research and without measuring or estimating any divergence. The question's own IDENTIFICATION_REQUIREMENTS demand, simultaneously: (1) an admissible JOB_POSTING corpus (LAB-OBJ-0019); (2) an independent source of HIRE events (LAB-OBJ-0022); and (3) a valid mechanism to compare or link the two. None is met within the sources and scope evaluated. (1) No admissible postings corpus exists: LAB-C1 and LAB-C1.1 evaluated eight candidates plus an ownership-check bundle against LAB-C0's own governance, applied as written, and both ruled NO_ADMISSIBLE_CANDIDATE_FOUND; LAB-Q-0014 was closed INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE on that limitation (LAB-CLM-0013); no posting was captured. (2) No admitted source observes HIRE events: LAB-OBJ-0022 remains DEFINED_PENDING_SOURCE with no observation mechanism, the Job Posting Observatory is NOT_SUPPORTED_FOR HIRE (LAB-SCM-0024) and was designed never to observe hiring outcomes, and LAB-B1 found no registration-flow (altas/bajas) data in any ARCA publication evaluated. Employment stocks (EMPLOYMENT_RELATIONSHIP, LAB-OBJ-0003) were not reinterpreted as hiring events, because HIRE is the transition event and not the resulting stock. (3) No validated linkage or common taxonomy connects the two sides: no admitted source shares a person-level or employer-level identifier with any other (LAB-CLM-0003, LAB-CLM-0011), and MLER's EMPLOYER/JOB fields are unrealized (GOV-006). The object-model distinctions POSTING != VACANCY != HIRE were preserved throughout: a posting was never treated as a vacancy, a vacancy was never treated as observable, and neither was treated as a hire. Because the question is conjunctive (both sides must be observable), the absence of either side alone would suffice; here both are absent. The conclusion is limited strictly to: there is not sufficient evidence, within the sources and scope evaluated, to compare postings with real hiring outcomes. This claim does not assert, and must not be read as asserting, that such evidence cannot exist outside this project's scope, and it deliberately does not use NOT_IDENTIFIABLE, which would assert a stronger structural impossibility than the current evidence supports.
